text:
**My pick for most RVs: a 2–3.5 kWh power station on a 400–800 W solar array.** The sources I could read didn't give bundle prices or confirm which panels go with which station, so check those yourself before buying.

**Pairings by RV type**

| RV type | Power station | Solar to pair | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Weekend or van/small trailer | [Jackery Explorer 1000 v2](https://amzn.to/463Djm2) (1,070 Wh, 1,500 W) | Two 200 W SolarSaga panels | The panels use its full 400 W solar input. Jackery often sells it as a package. |
| Fast charging, mid-size | [EcoFlow DELTA 3 Plus](https://amzn.to/45VmOIP) (1,024 Wh, 1,800 W) | Up to 1,000 W of panels on two inputs | It has the fastest recharge of the group, about 70 minutes with enough panels. |
| Multi-day boondocking | [BLUETTI AC200L](https://amzn.to/4qKjh9E) (2,048 Wh, 2,400 W) | Large array, up to 1,200 W | It has the highest solar input of the models I read about. |
| Longer stays with heavier loads | [Jackery Explorer 2000 v2](https://amzn.to/45ZSz3j) (2,042 Wh, 2,200 W) | Two 200 W panels | Jackery estimates about 7.5 hours to recharge. Solar input is capped at 400 W. |
| Larger rigs | [ALLPOWERS R4000](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-r4000-3456wh) (3,456 Wh, 3,600 W) | Panels on all three XT60 inputs, up to 2,000 W total | It has an RV outlet and a 5-year warranty. Solar panels aren't included. |

**ALLPOWERS R4000 price:** Code EXTRA12 brings it to $1,319.12, down from the $1,499 store price. It needs an order over $1,200 and expires 11/15/2026. I'm giving you the Dealectric link, and the site's price check was from 10/23. The checkout has the final say on price.

**Buying tips**
- **Match panel watts to the station's solar input limit.** Panels beyond the limit won't charge it faster.
- **Check panel voltage and connectors.** The R4000 takes 12–60 V per input.
- **Size by daily use.** A fridge, lights, a fan and device charging may fit in about 1 kWh a day. An RV air conditioner needs a much bigger setup.

**Caveats**
- The comparison pages I read were brand-level and thin on RV-specific testing.
- One page's three "check price" links all pointed to the same address, so I left them out.
- Tell me your daily power use, or whether you need to run the AC, and I can narrow this to one station and one panel set.

Sources: [Acquired Sense](https://www.acquiredsense.com/reviews/power-stations.html), [Smart Energy Edge](https://smartenergyedge.com/best-portable-power-station-with-solar-panels-for-camping/), [Dealectric](https://dealectric.com/lab/V8/allpowers-r4000-3456wh)
